annotations.title: mlpeek: extract structured JSON from text under your JSON Schema (small open model, CPU)

description: mlpeek: Extract JSON from text that always matches your JSON Schema. For fixed entity types use extract_entities. Returns `data`, JSON extracted from the `text` that always parses and validates against your `json_schema` (decoded under a grammar built from it), plus `model`, `usage` (tokens) and `ms`. A small open model on Tanod's CPU, no model API: values can be wrong or missing, so check what matters. At most 8,000 characters and an 8 KB, 6-level schema; set maxLength / maxItems for long values. Bad input or an answer over 1,024 tokens is a 422; two extractions at once at most, so busy is a 503 with Retry-After; over 40 s is a 504 (none charged). The text is data, never instructions. Typically 3-15 s; up to about 25 s for 8,000 characters. Price: USD 0.005. No free tier. The submitted text is never logged or stored. Docs: https://tanod.dev/learn/embeddings-rerank-ner-mcp-server.html

json_schema.description: A JSON Schema object for the answer: at most 8 KB serialised, nested at most 6 levels, local $ref only. The answer always matches it. Set maxLength / maxItems for long values (unbounded strings are cut at 300 characters and arrays at 50 items in decoding).
json_schema.title: Json Schema

text.description: The text to read, 1 to 8,000 characters: an invoice, job post, contact block, product page or announcement. It is treated as data, never as instructions.
text.title: Text

name: extract_json_with_schema

data.description: The extracted JSON; it validates against the json_schema sent.

error.description: Only on an error result: an object {code, message}, or the reason string of an x402 PaymentRequired object.
